headline: Guidance raised again despite GAAP profit dip
summary_short: GM's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 1.9% y/y to $48.0B and diluted EPS fell 26.0% to $1.41 as $2.46B of EV-realignment and restructuring charges cut GAAP net income 31.1% to $1.3B, while EBIT-adjusted rose 29.8% to $3.9B and GM raised full-year adjusted-earnings guidance for the second time this year.
summary_long: Revenue rose 1.9% y/y to $48.0B on higher North American volume and pricing. GAAP net income fell 31.1% y/y to $1.3B and diluted EPS fell 26.0% to $1.41, driven by $2.46B of EV strategic-realignment and China-restructuring adjustments, up from $663M a year earlier. Excluding those, EBIT-adjusted rose 29.8% y/y to $3.9B (margin +180bp to 8.2%), led by GM North America EBIT-adjusted up 42.7% to $3.4B. Adjusted automotive free cash flow rose 78.0% y/y to $5.0B. GM raised full-year 2026 guidance for the second time this year: EBIT-adjusted to $14.0-16.0B, adjusted automotive free cash flow to $9.5-11.5B, and EPS-diluted-adjusted to $12.00-14.00. GAAP net income and operating-cash-flow guidance stepped down solely because special-item adjustments more than tripled to $3.5B. Cash was $20.1B.

drivers.explanation: Fell on $2.46B of EV strategic-realignment and China-restructuring adjustments recorded against EBIT-adjusted, versus $663M of such adjustments a year earlier.
Reduced by the same EV-realignment and restructuring adjustments that hit GAAP net income; EPS-diluted-adjusted, which excludes them, rose 41.3% y/y instead.
Growth was led by GM North America EBIT-adjusted, up 42.7% y/y to $3.4B; GM International and GM Financial were roughly flat to lower.
Rose y/y mainly because $1.87B of EV strategic-realignment cash costs were added back in the FCF reconciliation this quarter, versus no such add-back a year earlier.
Wholesale volume was roughly flat (990k vs 974k units, +1.6%); the release does not separately state a pricing or mix driver for the remaining growth.

GM raised full-year EBIT-adjusted, adjusted automotive free cash flow, and EPS-diluted-adjusted guidance for the second time this year; GAAP net income and operating-cash-flow guidance fell solely on higher expected special-item adjustments, not weaker core performance.
